title: ZPC investigation and dashboards: query predicates, reports and the executive report

investigation-purpose.statement: Investigation runs queries on data collected by ZPC without creating alerts, and a result can be saved as an investigation or as a custom security policy.

quotes: You might want to glean certain information about your cloud deployment's posture without having to create alerts or filter information on the dashboard.
Run queries on the data collected by ZPC and gain more insight into your cloud deployment's security posture.
based on the result, save the investigation or create a custom security policy.

investigation-tabs.statement: On the Saved tab of the Investigation page ZPC shows when each query was last run (Last Run), and on the History tab each query Description.

quotes: On the Saved tab, you can do the following:
On the History tab, you can do the following:
Last Run: View when the query was last run.
Description: View the query description.

investigation-details-drawer.statement: A saved investigation has an Investigation Details drawer that shows the investigation query structure.

quotes: Each saved investigation has an Investigation Details drawer that shows the investigation query structure.

investigation-focus.statement: An investigation starts from a cloud type and a focus on either Assets or Identities.

quotes: Under Focus on, select either Assets or Identities.
2. Select your Cloud Type.

asset-network-predicates.statement: The asset relationship predicates are Can be accessed by Identity, Has Package and Has Identity, and the network access predicates are Internet Facing, Public Exposure Details and Publicly Accessible.

quotes: Can be accessed by Identity
Has Package
Has Identity
Internet Facing
Public Exposure Details
Publicly Accessible

property-operators-by-type.statement: Asset property predicate operators depend on the property type; Boolean accepts = and ≠, and Date accepts =, <= (Before or on) and >= (After or on).

quotes: | Boolean | = : Is ≠ : Is not |
| Date | = : Is <= : Before or on >= : After or on |

metadata-consolidation.statement: ZPC consolidates asset attributes from the cloud service providers into asset metadata; for example, hard drives connected to EC2s are collected and presented as part of the metadata although AWS does not include them in the EC2 metadata.

quotes: ZPC ensures a holistic metadata by consolidating the attributes of each asset from the cloud service providers on asset details.
information regarding hard drives connected to EC2s is not part of the EC2 metadata on AWS, but ZPC collects the information and presents it as part of the metadata.

k8s-running-predicate.statement: One asset predicate returns true if the Kubernetes cluster is running, and the page says it is only available for investigating Kubernetes clusters.

quotes: Returns true if the kubernetes cluster is running. Accepts the following operator:
This predicate is only available for investigating Kubernetes clusters.
evidence.after: Returns true if the kubernetes cluster is running. Accepts the following operator:

vuln-and-data-predicates.statement: One asset predicate returns true if the asset has at least one vulnerability found by the ZPC vulnerability scanner, and another returns true if the asset has at least one file containing sensitive data detected by the ZPC data security scan.

quotes: Returns true if the asset has at least one vulnerability found by the ZPC vulnerability scanner.
Returns true if the asset has at least one file containing sensitive data detected by the ZPC data security scan.

aws-password-predicate.statement: An identity authentication predicate returns Yes if the IAM user has a password, No if it does not, and Unknown for identities ZPC has no visibility into, and the page says it is available only for AWS identity focus queries.

quotes: Returns "Yes" if the IAM user has a password, "No" if the IAM user does not have a password, and "Unknown" for identities that ZPC does not have visibility into.
Available only for AWS identity focus queries.
evidence.after: You can use the following identity authentication predicates:

access-key-15-minute.statement: For AWS, when an access key is used more than once in a 15-minute span, only the first use is recorded in the field behind the predicates for the access key last-used timestamp, region and service.

quotes: Returns the timestamp for AWS local identities that used an access key to sign an AWS API request. When an access key is used more than once in a 15-minute span, only the first use is recorded in this field on AWS.
Returns the AWS Region where the access key was most recently used. When an access key is used more than once in a 15-minute span, only the first use is recorded in this field on AWS.
Returns the AWS Service in which the access key was most recently used to access. When an access key is used more than once in a 15-minute span, only the first use is recorded in this field on AWS.

power-predicates.statement: One identity predicate returns a numerical value between 1-100 which is the identity power score, and another returns true if the power score for the identity is above 80.

quotes: Returns a numerical value between 1-100 which is the identity's power score.
Returns true if the power score for the identity is above 80.

investigation-results.statement: Investigation results can be exported as an Excel file; identity-focused results include Used(%), the entitlement count percentage the identity is accessing, and Last Activity.

quotes: Export the investigation result as an excel file.
Used(%): View the entitlement count percentage which the identity is accessing.
Last Activity: View the time stamp for when the identity performed it's last activity.

threats-categories.statement: The Cloud Threats Dashboard groups alerts into Security Event (security events that have already occurred, such as crypto mining or suspicious activity) and Security Exposure (potential exposure, such as dormant accounts or authentication misconfiguration).

quotes: Security Event: Alerts triggered for security events that have already occurred in the cloud deployment such as crypto mining, suspicious activity, etc.
Security Exposure: Alerts triggered for potential exposure to security events such as dormant accounts, authentication misconfiguration, etc.

threats-ranges.statement: The Cloud Threats Dashboard Alerts by Risk Level chart offers durations of last 7, 15, 30, 60, 90 or 180 days, while the security event trend covers the last 7 days and its top policies list shows the top 5.

quotes: Alerts by Risk Level: View open low, medium, high, and critical alerts with an assigned theme of Security Events or Security Exposure (Threat Category) for the selected duration (last 7 days, last 15 days, last 30 days, last 60 days, last 90 days, or last 180 days).
Alerts Trend: View all the alerts for the selected security event category for the last 7 days.
Top Policies: View the top 5 policies related to the security event category with the highest number of alerts.

assets-dash-ranges.statement: The Cloud Assets Dashboard Cloud Type Trend offers durations of last 7, 15, 30, 60 or 90 days, and it lists the top 10 asset types and top 10 asset categories by number of assets.

quotes: Cloud Type Trend: View asset distribution across all cloud types for the selected duration (last 7 days, last 15 days, last 30 days, last 60 days, last 90 days).
View Top 10 Asset Types by Asset: View top 10 Asset Types with the highest number of assets.
View Top 10 Categories by Assets: View top 10 Asset Categories with the highest number of assets.

assets-dash-status.statement: On the Cloud Assets Dashboard an asset fails even if a single security policy against it fails, risk level is Low, Medium, High or Critical based on open alerts, and the total asset count is the number of assets ingested by ZPC for metadata collection.

quotes: An asset fails even if a single security policy against it fails.
View the total number of assets evaluated based on the risk level of open alerts.
Asset risk level is separated into Low, Medium, High, and Critical.
The total number of assets is the total number of assets ingested by ZPC in terms of metadata collection.

identities-dash-ranges.statement: The Cloud Identities Dashboard All Identities trend offers durations of last 7, 15, 30, 60 or 90 days, and it shows top 10 roles and top 10 accounts by identity count and top 10 identities by resource count.

quotes: All Identities: View all local, federated, external identities and their alerts for the selected duration (last 7 days, last 15 days, last 30 days, last 60 days, or last 90 days).
View Roles by Number of Identities: View top 10 roles by identity count.
View Accounts by Number of Identities: View top 10 accounts by identity count.
View Identities by Number of Resources: View top 10 identities by resource count.

identities-dash-federated.statement: The Cloud Identities Dashboard describes federated identities as users defined on a user directory such as Okta who are authorized to use cloud service providers, and says a removed federated user loses all roles and permissions.

quotes: Federated: Users that are defined on your user directory such as Okta, and are authorized to use cloud service providers.
When you remove a federated user from your organization, they lose all roles and permissions.

iac-dash.statement: The IaC Dashboard shows policy violations by scan plugin and by cloud type categorized by severity, and clicking a scan plugin opens the Alerts > All Alerts List tab filtered by that plugin.

quotes: View Policy Violations via Scan Plugin. The policy violation count for all IaC scanner plugins across your CI/CD tools such as GitHub.
Click the scan plugin to view the policy on the Alerts > All Alerts List tab.
The policy is filtered based on the scan plugin selected.
The Policy violation count for each cloud service provider and Kubernetes categorized by severity.

vuln-dash-scope.statement: The Vulnerability Dashboard covers container registry and cloud workload vulnerabilities across AWS, Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud Platform, correlated with CVEs from the national vulnerability database and prioritized by CVSS score.

quotes: The Vulnerability Dashboard offers insight into your container registry and cloud workload vulnerability across Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud Platform (GCP).
This dashboard displays the detected vulnerabilities correlated with the common vulnerabilities and exposure (CVE) defined in the national vulnerability database (NVD) database
prioritizes the vulnerabilities and the associated risk based on the common vulnerability scoring system (CVSS) score.

vuln-dash-ranges-severity.statement: On the Container Registry Images tab of the Vulnerability Dashboard, the time range is 1, 7, 15 or 30 days and the severity levels Critical, High, Medium, Low and Unknown are determined from the CVSS score.

quotes: Time Range: Select 1 day, 7 days, 15 days, or 30 days.
View the vulnerability count categorized by severity (Critical, High, Medium, Low, Unknown). The severity is determined based on the CVSS score.

compliance-dash.statement: The Compliance Dashboard shows policy compliance trends over the last 7, 15, 30, 60 or 90 days for the selected benchmark, and benchmark title, policy count and compliance score for laws and regulations and custom benchmarks.

quotes: Policy Compliance: View the passed and failed policy trend for the selected benchmark and selected duration (last 7 days, last 15 days, last 30 days, last 60 days, last 90 days).
View Laws & Regulations Benchmark Compliance: View benchmark title, policy count, and compliance score for each law & regulation benchmark.
View Custom Benchmark: View benchmark title, policy count, and compliance score for each custom benchmark.

excel-report-types.statement: Excel reports can be downloaded for Cloud Alerts, IaC Alerts, Cloud Assets and Vulnerabilities, while compliance reports are scheduled and generated.

quotes: You can download Excel reports for:
To download a cloud alerts or an IaC alerts report:
To download a Cloud Asset report:
To download a vulnerability report:
You can schedule and generate Compliance reports.

report-download-pending.statement: In the alerts report download steps, a requested report that is not yet generated shows the status Pending.

quotes: If the report is not yet generated, then the status shows as Pending.

scheduled-reports-purpose.statement: The About Scheduled Reports page says ZPC can view or schedule reports for all available benchmarks, and that the Scheduled Reports page (Administration > Scheduled Reports) lists the scheduled compliance reports and creates new ones; the Enabling or Disabling page describes schedules that generate "compliance or alert" reports.

quotes: ZPC offers you to view or schedule reports for all available benchmarks.
View all the scheduled compliance reports.
Create a new compliance report.
On the Scheduled Reports page (Administration > Scheduled Reports), you can:
After you've created a specific schedule to generate the compliance or alert reports, you can choose to enable or disable the schedule.

scheduled-reports-actions.statement: On the Scheduled Reports page a schedule can be searched in the searchable columns and edited or deleted, and the visible table columns can be chosen.

quotes: 2. Search for a specific schedule report in the searchable columns.
You can choose which columns appear on the report table.
4. Edit or delete a schedule report.

scheduled-reports-edit-delete.statement: A reporting schedule can be edited by choosing the Edit icon for the fields to change, or deleted after a confirmation message, from Administration > Scheduled Reports.

quotes: You can edit or delete a reporting schedule when required.
3. Click the Edit icon for the fields you want to edit.
1. Go to Administration > Scheduled Reports.
2. Click the Delete icon for the scheduled report that you want to delete.
3. A confirmation message appears. Click Delete.

scheduled-compliance-report.statement: A scheduled compliance report has a unique name, an Excel or PDF format, one or more active benchmarks, and recipient email addresses.

quotes: Schedule Name: Enter a unique name for the report.
Format: Select either Excel or PDF.
Benchmark: Select one or multiple active compliance benchmarks.
Recipients: Enter the email addresses of the recipients.

schedule-warning-icon.statement: A warning icon appears next to the Schedule Name if there is an issue with the schedule scope, such as the assigned Business Unit having been deleted.

quotes: A warning icon appears next to the Schedule Name if there is an issue with the schedule scope (e.g., the Business Unit assigned to the scheduled report was deleted).

schedule-default-enabled.statement: A compliance or alert report schedule is enabled by default when first created, and disabling it pauses the report from being generated and sent to the recipient.

quotes: After you've created a specific schedule to generate the compliance or alert reports, you can choose to enable or disable the schedule.
By default, the schedule is enabled when you first create a report schedule.
This option allows you to pause the report from being generated and sent to the recipient for a specific duration.

exec-report-purpose.statement: The Executive Report is a high-level overview for executives of cloud account security posture and mitigation progress, which can be shared as a PDF.

quotes: The report is for executives (managers, VPs, etc.) to get a high-level overview of the security posture of the cloud accounts and the progress related to mitigating the security issues
share the report in PDF format with the executives.

exec-report-ranges-defaults.statement: Executive report asset status can be viewed for the last 7, 15 or 30 days, and asset status and cloud alerts display the last 7 days by default.

quotes: Select the duration for which you want to view the asset status (Last 7 days, Last 15 days, Last 30 days).
By default, the status is displayed for the last 7 days.
By default, the alerts are displayed for the last 7 days.

exec-report-selection-limits.statement: In the executive report, up to five policies can be selected at a time for Open Alerts by Policy and up to five benchmarks for Compliance.

quotes: Open Alerts by Policy: The total number of open alerts for the specific policy for the selected duration (Last 7 days, Last 15 days, Last 30 days). You can select up to five policies at a time.
Compliance: The compliance score for the specific benchmark for the selected duration (Last 7 days, Last 15 days, Last 30 days). You can select up to five benchmarks at a time.

exec-report-top10.statement: The executive report ranks the top 10 risky accounts by number of critical alerts, the top 10 failed resource types, and the top 10 accounts by number of resources.

quotes: Top 10 Risky Accounts by Open Alerts: The top 10 accounts at risk based on the highest number of critical alerts associated with each account.
Top 10 Failed Resources: The top 10 failed resource types (S3, EC2, etc.).
Top 10 Accounts by Assets: The top 10 accounts with the highest number of resources.

exec-report-scanned.statement: The executive report shows the number of cloud workloads scanned for known vulnerabilities, and Vulnerability Images Scanned is an average.

quotes: Vulnerability Workloads Scanned: The number of cloud workloads scanned for known vulnerabilities.
Vulnerability Images Scanned: The average number of images scanned to detect known vulnerabilities.

exec-schedule.statement: A scheduled executive report has a unique schedule name, a report that defaults to the default Executive Report page, recipients, and an Enabled or Disabled status.

quotes: Schedule Name: Enter a unique name for the report.
Recipients: Enter the email addresses of the recipients.
By default, the default Executive Report page is selected.
Status: Select the status (Enabled or Disabled) to enable or disable scheduling.

exec-save-options.statement: Editing a saved executive report offers Save as New Report, which saves the edit as another customized report, or Save Changes.

quotes: Save as New Report: Click to save the edited report as another customized report.
Save Changes: Click to save the report.

exec-scheduled-editable.statement: A scheduled executive report can be edited by changing the Schedule Name, Report, Recipients, Status or Frequency.

quotes: change the Schedule Name, Report, Recipients, Status, or Frequency as required.

report-generation-limits.title: Report generation time, retention and size limits
report-generation-limits.detail: Beyond the status Pending, no captured page gives a generation time, My Downloads retention, or size and row limits for Excel and PDF exports, nor limits on saved investigations, History retention, scheduled reports or recipients per schedule.

alert-status-definitions.title: What each alert status means
alert-status-definitions.detail: Alert status is Open, Closed or Resolved on the identity and policy Alerts tabs and adds Ignored on the asset Alerts tab, but these pages do not define each status. zpc.alerts:status-values defines Open, Closed, Resolved and Reopened, and does not list Ignored or say whether the Alerts tab values match it.

api-coverage.title: Whether ZPC investigations, reports and dashboards have API, SDK or Terraform coverage
api-coverage.detail: The ZPC API as captured in zpc.api covers alerts only. Source classes not checked: SDK and Terraform provider coverage of policies, benchmarks, ignore rules, investigations and reports.

service-status.title: Whether the ZPC features these pages describe are still available
service-status.detail: portfolio.cloud-protection records ZPC end of life as planned for March 15, 2026 (portfolio.cloud-protection:zpc-eos-eol). None of the captured investigation, dashboard or report pages says whether it describes a service still available, so none of these facts is claimed as current.
